verses.text: You, LORD God, are my protector. Rescue me and keep me safe from all who chase me.

footnotes.text: Psalm 7 Written by David: The Hebrew text has “a shiggaion by David,” which may refer to a psalm of mourning.

verses.text: Or else they will rip me apart like lions attacking a victim, and no one will save me.
I have not betrayed a friend or had pity on an enemy who attacks for no reason.

footnotes.text: had pity on an enemy: Or “failed to have pity on an enemy.”

verses.text: If I have done any of this, then let my enemies chase and capture me. Let them trample me to death and leave me in the dirt.
Get angry, LORD God! Do something! Attack my furious enemies. See that justice is done.
Make the nations come to you, as you sit on your throne above them all.

footnotes.text: sit … throne: Or “return to your place.”

verses.text: Our LORD, judge the nations! Judge me and show that I am honest and innocent.
You know every heart and mind, and you always do right. Now make violent people stop, but protect all of us who obey you.
You, God, are my shield, the protector of everyone whose heart is right.
You see that justice is done, and each day you take revenge.
Whenever your enemies refuse to change their ways, you sharpen your sword and string your bow.
Your deadly arrows are ready with flaming tips.
An evil person is like a woman about to give birth to a hateful, deceitful, and rebellious child.
Such people dig a deep hole, then fall in it themselves.
The trouble they cause comes back on them, and their heads are crushed by their own evil deeds.
I will praise you, LORD! You always do right. I will sing about you, the LORD Most High.
